text: John 1 so far presents Jesus as the eternal Word of God, who existed with God in the beginning and is Himself God. He is the Creator of all things, the source of life and light, and the one who shines in the darkness, overcoming it. John the Baptist came as a witness to testify about this light, but the world—even His own people—did not recognize or receive Him. Yet, those who did receive Him were given the right to become God’s children, not by human effort but by God’s will. Now, in verse 14, we see the profound truth that the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, revealing His glory as the one and only Son of the Father, full of grace and truth.

text:
Psalm 119, from verse 48 through the current verse (150), is a heartfelt meditation on God’s Word, written as an acrostic poem in Hebrew. The psalmist expresses deep love, devotion, and dependence on Scripture, even in the face of affliction, persecution, and mockery. Here’s a summary of the passage so far:

The psalmist repeatedly declares their commitment to God’s commandments, statutes, and precepts, calling them their delight, comfort, and source of wisdom. Despite hardship—such as being mocked by the arrogant, bound by wicked schemes, or feeling faint with longing for salvation—the psalmist clings to God’s Word as their anchor. They find hope, life, and understanding in Scripture, even when surrounded by those who forsake it.

The psalmist acknowledges God’s righteousness and faithfulness, recognizing that affliction has refined their faith and drawn them closer to obedience. They ask for mercy, understanding, and deliverance, trusting that God’s Word is true and unchanging. The passage is filled with declarations of love for God’s law, even when it brings conviction or challenges from others. The psalmist also expresses a longing for God’s nearness and justice, crying out for salvation and revival according to His promises.

In short, this section of Psalm 119 is a passionate love letter to God’s Word, showing how Scripture sustains, guides, and comforts the believer in every circumstance.
